strengths: EA-KD offers a simple, practical weighting rule that combines teacher and student entropy without auxiliary networks or additional inference cost. Its compatibility with both logit and feature distillation is useful.

The classification evidence is broad: Table 2 reports improvements in 46 of 49 framework–architecture combinations, averaging 0.56 percentage points. Improvements over vanilla KD include 3.39 points on Tiny-ImageNet and 0.76 points on ImageNet.

Transformer-to-CNN experiments and COCO detection results support applicability beyond conventional CNN classification. The detection improvements of 0.81 and 1.68 AP over KD are meaningful; the GPT-2 experiments provide additional evidence of transferability.

The manuscript includes component and temperature ablations, comparisons with related entropy weighting, and repeated-run statistics in the supplement. Relevant methods and datasets are credited, and a code repository is identified. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-4n6lxdir/call-71940b968f2e4d27a452c5736eaf6b1c/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The experiments do not isolate sample prioritization from overall loss rescaling. Equations 12–14 use weights that are not normalized to unit mean, changing the effective KD coefficient and its evolution during training. Section 4.1 also reduces the MLD+LS coefficient from 9 to 4. Controls using matched constant weights, normalized weights, and comparable coefficient tuning are needed to establish how much improvement comes specifically from adaptive sample weighting.

The distinctive contribution beyond existing uncertainty weighting is only moderately supported. Appendix A.1 acknowledges that WTTM already emphasizes uncertain samples and discusses teacher entropy. In Table 9, adding student adaptation improves teacher-only weighting by just 0.32, 0.18, and 0.08 points, and slightly worsens FCFD. EA-TTM exceeds WTTM by only 0.03–0.19 points in Table A1. Appendix C reports EA variability but relies on published baseline means for the main comparisons, leaving several small advantages uncertain.

The explanation that high entropy identifies valuable knowledge is stronger than the evidence establishes. Equations 5–7 demonstrate KL behavior for a uniformly initialized student; zero divergence between matching uniform distributions does not establish harmful optimization bias. High predictive entropy can also reflect teacher uncertainty or error. The t-SNE visualizations do not identify actual classifier boundaries, and the asserted connection between feature magnitude and low entropy is unsupported. These analyses motivate a heuristic but do not validate the claimed general mechanism.

Important implementation choices remain unspecified. Whether student entropy is detached from backpropagation changes the objective: differentiating through the weight introduces an additional entropy-gradient term beyond weighted KD. The manuscript also lacks precise definitions of entropy aggregation and weighting for detection proposals and language-model sequences. These details are necessary to reproduce the claimed extensions and interpret their results.
